# Sources of the image fixtures and the official sample payloads

## Images in this directory

Every PNG and PDF here was **generated by `test/fixtures/generate.rb`**. The
script renders the payloads with `rqrcode` 3.2 (error correction level M, byte
mode, quiet zone of 4 modules), as IG §6.1 requires. It then checks that
`QrReader.decode_all` returns exactly the expected texts for each file.
`expected.json` maps each file to the payload fixtures it contains. Entries of
the form `{"not_a_bill": "..."}` are QR codes that are not QR-bills and that
`SwissQr.read_all` has to skip. Codes on a multi-code page come back in no
guaranteed order, so compare them as sets.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `six_ig_ex1_qrr.png`, `six_ig_ex2_qrr_swico_two_alt_procedures.png` | Official SIX sample payloads (see below), rendered by us |
| `iban_scor_eur.png`, `combined_address_k_legacy.png`, `unicode_charset.png` | Hand-built payloads |
| `max_lengths.png` | Largest valid payload (869 characters, QR version 24; the spec maximum of 997 characters gives version 25) |
| `qriban_qrr_lf_swiss_cross.png` | With the Swiss cross drawn over the centre, as on a printed QR-bill (error correction repairs it) |
| `bill_and_url.png` | One QR-bill and one unrelated URL code side by side |
| `url_only.png` | Only an unrelated URL code (`SwissQr.read` should return nil) |
| `invoice_two_pages.pdf` | Hand-written, Flate-compressed PDF with two A4 pages. The codes are vector rectangles at 46 x 46 mm with the Swiss cross. Page 1 has one bill. Page 2 has a bill and a small URL code. |

**No SIX image or PDF is included.** All SIX documents say "All rights are
reserved with respect to this document, including with regard to photocopying
and storage on electronic media" (© SIX Interbank Clearing Ltd / SIX Group Ltd),
and no licence for redistribution is given. That makes redistribution unclear,
so it is skipped. To test against the originals, download them from the URLs
below. They are freely available.

## Official sample payloads (`payloads/valid/six_*.txt`)

The `six_*` payloads hold the **verbatim data encoded in the QR codes that SIX
prints in its public documents**. They are not taken from the text tables
beside those codes, because the tables differ from the codes in several places
(see "Differences" below). Method, run 2026-10-14:

1. Download the PDFs below.
2. Render the pages with `pdftoppm -r 250..300`.
3. Decode with `QrReader.decode_all` (qr_reader 0.0.2).
4. Deduplicate.

`generate.rb` holds each decoded string (`OFFICIAL_VERBATIM`) and the field list
it represents (`OFFICIAL`). On every run it rebuilds the payload from the fields
and requires a byte-for-byte match. The data itself is SIX's fictitious sample
data: sample IBANs and names such as "Max Muster & Söhne, Seldwyla".

| Document | URL | SHA-256 of the file used |
|---|---|---|
| Swiss Implementation Guidelines for the QR-bill, v2.4 (24.02.2026, valid from 14 Nov 2026), EN | https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/banking-services/standardization/qr-bill/ig-qr-bill-v2.4-en.pdf | `a41e5887a4a2d16a060519014cebd1cf739c3d51d6ec74815bb7531659d38e17` |
| Same, v2.2 (22.02.2021), EN: same codes as v2.4 Annex A, plus the field-label code on p. 40 | https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/banking-services/standardization/qr-bill/ig-qr-bill-v2.2-en.pdf | `63b80b2d8fc4d52261a8d4ac3fb721e7c34264f397dffa69a68ad57cf67997da` |
| Style Guide QR-bill v1.1 (valid from 01.01.2026), EN | https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/banking-services/standardization/qr-bill/style-guide-qr-bill-en.pdf | `d4aed6873cc118a148e134658df2ebb64f9846157a8f871fbfb36608563aab16` |
| Introduction script QR-bill for invoice issuers and recipients v1.1 (April 2021), EN | https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/banking-services/standardization/qr-bill/introduction-script-invoice-issuers-recipients-en.pdf | `e78b9461e20bed75d93b146ac34ed9dc1d846017ab755e33d5200620a53ef160` |
| Alternative procedures v1.0 (20.05.2022), EN | https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/banking-services/standardization/qr-bill/alternative-procedures-en.pdf | `84ea1447ae9ebf705a54cda53451f6ace7457885dbff689a8da5c2bd21d967b0` |

Each fixture's `.json` names its exact page(s) in `_source`.

### Differences between SIX's QR codes and their text tables

- **IG Annex A example 4:** the table and the printed payment part show the
  creditor reference `RF72 0191 2301 0040 5JSH 0438`, whose ISO 11649 check
  digits are **wrong** (mod 97 = 49). The QR code on the same page encodes
  `RF240191230100405JSH0438`, which is correct. The valid fixture uses the QR
  value. `payloads/invalid/six_ig_ex4_table_scor_typo.txt` uses the table value.
- **IG v2.4 example 2:** the table lists one alternative procedure,
  `eBill/B/simon.muster@example.com`. The QR code carries two placeholders,
  `Name AV1: UV;UltraPay005;12345` and `Name AV2: XY;XYService;54321`.
- **IG v2.4 examples 1 and 3:** the tables say "Max Muster & Söhne (sample
  company)", "Muster Stiftung (sample foundation)" and "P.O. box". The QR codes
  say "Max Muster & Söhne", "Sample Foundation" and "PO Box".
- **Style guide and introduction script codes:** the debtor street is
  `"Musterstrasse "`, with a trailing blank.
- **Trailing separators:** 6 of the 18 official codes end with `EPD\n` or
  `EPD\r\n`, although IG §4.1.4 says "The carriage return after the final
  element is eliminated". Some use CRLF and some LF.

## Searched for but not found

- A freely licensed, downloadable sample QR-bill PDF or PNG from SIX. The only
  official samples are inside the copyrighted documents above.
  paymentstandards.ch now redirects to six-group.com. The old
  "sample files 1.1.1-3.4.4" set that the introduction script refers to is not
  offered for download anywhere I could find.
- Any official sample with a combined ("K") address. The current documents
  contain none, so `combined_address_k_*` are hand-built from the IG v2.2 rules.
